name.description: A user-defined name of the function. Function names must be unique globally.
name.rationale: Name has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

runtime.description: Eg. `"nodejs20"`, `"python39"`, `"dotnet3"`, `"go116"`, `"java11"`, `"ruby30"`, `"php74"`, etc. Check the [official doc](https://cloud.google.com/functions/docs/concepts/exec#runtimes) for the up-to-date list. - - -
runtime.rationale: Only fully supporterd runtimes should be used ensuring there are no vulnerabilities, outdated libraries and not decomissioned or depreciate

description.rationale: Description has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

available_memory_mb.description: Memory (in MB), available to the function.
available_memory_mb.rationale: How much memory the cloud function get effects performance, can cause crashes which can lead to security risks

timeout.rationale: A timeout value being too short or too long can leave the cloud function vulnerable

entry_point.description: Name of the function that will be executed when the Google Cloud Function is triggered.
entry_point.rationale: entry_point name has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

event_trigger.description: A source that fires events in response to a condition in another service.
event_trigger.rationale: event_trigger cannot be used with trigger http, which a policy has been written for

event_type.description: See the documentation on [calling Cloud Functions](https://cloud.google.com/functions/docs/calling/) for a full reference of accepted triggers.
event_type.rationale: event_trigger cannot be used with trigger http, which a policy has been written for

resource.description: which to observe events. For example, `"myBucket"` or `"projects/my-project/topics/my-topic"`
resource.rationale: event_trigger cannot be used with trigger http, which a policy has been written for

failure_policy.rationale: event_trigger cannot be used with trigger http, which a policy has been written for

https_trigger_security_level.description: * `SECURE_ALWAYS` Requests for a URL that match this handler that do not use HTTPS are automatically redirected to the HTTPS URL with the same path. Query parameters are reserved for the redirect. * `SECURE_OPTIONAL` Both HTTP and HTTPS requests with URLs that match the handler succeed without redirects. The application can examine the request to determine which protocol was used and respond accordingly.
https_trigger_security_level.rationale: http trigger security level should always be enforced

ingress_settings.description: String value that controls what traffic can reach the function.
ingress_settings.rationale: allowing internal traffic prevents untrusted access to the GCP environment

labels.description: **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration. Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: labels has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

terraform_labels.description: The combination of labels configured directly on the resource and default labels configured on the provider.
terraform_labels.rationale: terraform labels has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

effective_labels.description: All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.
effective_labels.rationale: labels has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

service_account_email.description: If provided, the self-provided service account to run the function with.
service_account_email.security_impact: A provided email has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

build_service_account.description: If provided, the self-provided service account to use to build the function
build_service_account.rationale: A provided email to build the service account has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

environment_variables.description: A set of key/value environment variable pairs to assign to the function.
environment_variables.rationale: environment variabls pairs being assigned has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

build_environment_variables.description: A set of key/value environment variable pairs available during build time.
build_environment_variables.rationale: if environment vaiablea are not being used, there is no reason to build the environment variables

build_worker_pool.description: Name of the Cloud Build Custom Worker Pool that should be used to build the function.
build_worker_pool.rationale: Naming the cloud build custom worker pool has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

vpc_connector.description: The VPC Network Connector that this cloud function can connect to
vpc_connector.rationale: The VPC connector has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

vpc_connector_egress_settings.description: The egress settings for the connector, controlling what traffic is diverted through it.
vpc_connector_egress_settings.rationale: Allowing all extneral traffic to go through VPC connector can cause security risks such as data breaching

source_archive_bucket.description: The GCS bucket containing the zip archive which contains the function.
source_archive_bucket.rationale: The bucket containing the zip archive has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

source_archive_object.description: The source archive object (file) in archive bucket.
source_archive_object.rationale: The source achive file has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

source_repository.description: Cannot be set alongside `source_archive_bucket` or `source_archive_object`. Structure is [documented below](#nested_source_repository). It must match the pattern `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/repositories/{repository}`.*
source_repository.rationale: The source repository does not have an impact on the security of the resource or the data contained

url.description: * To refer to a specific commit: `https://source.developers.google.com/projects/*/repos/*/revisions/*/paths/*` * To refer to a moveable alias (branch): `https://source.developers.google.com/projects/*/repos/*/moveable-aliases/*/paths/*`. To refer to HEAD, use the `master` moveable alias. * To refer to a specific fixed alias (tag): `https://source.developers.google.com/projects/*/repos/*/fixed-aliases/*/paths/*`
url.rationale: The URL points to user defined repositories, projects and revisions, the security of source repository will relate back to the region it resides in

docker_registry.description: Docker Registry to use for storing the function's Docker images
docker_registry.rationale: CONTAINER_REGISTRY has been depreciated and can therefore cause security risks to the resource and its data

docker_repository.rationale: docker registry will be automatically set to artifact registry to prevent security risks to the resource and its data

kms_key_name.description: If specified, you must also provide an artifact registry repository using the `docker_repository` field that was created with the same KMS crypto key. Before deploying, please complete all pre-requisites described in https://cloud.google.com/functions/docs/securing/cmek#granting_service_accounts_access_to_the_key
kms_key_name.rationale: A docker repository field needs to be set for kms key name to be active and therefor does not pose security risks to the resource and its data

max_instances.description: The limit on the maximum number of function instances that may coexist at a given time.
max_instances.rationale: Too many instances can result in exaustion and open security risks

min_instances.description: he limit on the minimum number of function instances that may coexist at a given time.
min_instances.rationale: A minimum number of instances has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained only maximum

secret_environment_variables.rationale: secret environment variables have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

key.rationale: Name of the environment variable has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

project_id.rationale: A project ID has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

secret.rationale: An ID of a secret has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

version.rationale: Secret environment variables are not implemented and therefroe the version of the secret has no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

secret_volumes.rationale: Secret volumes have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

mount_path.description: The path within the container to mount the secret volume.
mount_path.rationale: Secret volumes are not configured and therefore mount paths have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

project_id.rationale: Secret volumes are not configured and therefore project ID have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

secret.description: ID of the secret in secret manager
secret.rationale: Secret volumes are not configured and therefore secrets have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

versions.description: List of secret versions to mount for this secret.
versions.rationale: Secret volumes are not configured and therefore versions have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

automatic_update_policy.description: Security patches are applied automatically to the runtime without requiring the function to be redeployed
automatic_update_policy.rationale: automatic updates can patch security misconfigurations and therefore protect the security of the resource or the data contained

on_deploy_update_policy.description: Security patches are only applied when a function is redeployed.
on_deploy_update_policy.rationale: can not be used with automatic update policy

runtime_version.description: The runtime version which was used during latest function deployment.
runtime_version.rationale: because automatic update policy is functioning, on deploy update policy cannot and therefore runtime version does not apose security threats to the resource or the data contained

retry.description: Whether the function should be retried on failure.
retry.rationale: If a function fails, it should try to be restarted to ensure data is not lost or corrupted

versions.description: List of secret versions to mount for this secret
versions.rationale: secret versions have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

path.description: Relative path of the file under the mount path where the secret value for this version will be fetched and made available.
path.rationale: descriptions of secret versions have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.

version.rationale: The version of secrets have no impact on the security of the resource or the data contained.
